headline: SEMICON India 2026 Day 2 Highlights India’s Semiconductor Journey from Ambition to Execution at Scale
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

SEMICON India 2026 Day 2 Highlights India’s Semiconductor Journey from Ambition to Execution at Scale

Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw highlights ISM 2.0, indigenous design, manufacturing, talent and India’s emergence as a trusted global semiconductor partner

R&D, resilient supply chains, product innovation and international partnerships strengthen India’s ‘Silicon to Systems’ ecosystem

18 SEP 2026 10:12PM by PIB Delhi

The second day of SEMICON India 2026 at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, brought together policymakers, global semiconductor leaders, Indian industry, researchers, startups, academia and students for deliberations spanning manufacturing, supply chains, Research and Development (R&D), international partnerships, chip design, advanced packaging, materials and talent, reflecting India’s progress towards an integrated and globally competitive “Silicon to Systems” ecosystem.

In a fireside conversation, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics & Information Technology, Railways, and Information & Broadcasting, said India’s semiconductor mission has moved from proving intent to execution at scale. He said ISM 2.0 would build on the foundation created under ISM 1.0 through six pillars—Design; Machines and Materials; Setting up More Fabs; Strengthening the ATMP/OSAT Industry; Research and Development; and Talent Development. The Minister said that ISM 1.0, originally envisaged as a six-year programme, achieved its objectives in just four years, and expressed confidence that ISM 2.0 would similarly progress ahead of schedule, supported by strong and growing investor interest.

Highlighting design as one of India’s core strengths, the Minister estimated at least 200 chip design companies emerging under ISM 2.0, calling it a “game changer” for building home grown semiconductor IP. More than 105 chip design startups gained access to state-of-the-art Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools, with 20 startups securing venture capital funding. Around 70,000 chip-design engineers have been trained in four years, against a target of training 85,000 design engineers. The Minister emphasised that global competitiveness requires both quality and competitive cost, and highlighted that five plants out the twelve plants approved under ISM 1.0 have commenced commercial production. The Minister also underlined India’s recognition as a trusted country and its strong record in intellectual property protection.

During his interaction with the media, Shri Vaishnaw highlighted the strong domestic and international response to SEMICON India 2026, extensive business-to-business engagements and significant participation from major semiconductor economies. He said the Country Roundtables demonstrated growing interest among global companies in expanding their engagement with India. The Minister also highlighted the transition from design services towards a “Product Nation”, with Indian-designed chips increasingly moving into end products. He emphasised machines and materials, specialised semiconductor logistics, sustainability, water recycling and industry-ready talent as important elements of the emerging ecosystem.

Day 2 also witnessed 25 MoUs/Announcements and strategic collaborations across semiconductor materials, manufacturing, power electronics, advanced packaging, logistics, design and skilling involving Indian and global ecosystem partners. The initiatives covered localisation of critical materials, indigenous Silicon Carbide power technologies, semiconductor design tools, deep-tech investment, specialised logistics and workforce development, further strengthening domestic capabilities across the semiconductor value chain.

Foreign Secretary Shri Vikram Misri emphasized that resilient semiconductor value chains require trusted global partnerships. He highlighted reliability, credibility, incentives and value creation as pillars of cooperation, and called for a balanced approach to self-reliance based on domestic strengths combined with global capabilities.

The ‘Supply Chain 360’ Panel discussion focused on localisation of critical inputs and resilient supply networks.

Shri Ruchir Dixit, Siemens EDA, highlighted the need to address AI-driven compute growth through advanced architecture, 3D ICs, packaging and chip-system co-design.

Shri Gokul V. Subramaniam, Intel, detailed AI applications across RTL generation, verification, floorplanning, power analysis, clock-tree synthesis and physical design, positioning AI as an optimisation engine for increasingly complex chips.

A panel on ‘From Concept to Silicon’ discussed strengthening India’s design enablement and test ecosystem. Speakers emphasised access to EDA tools, prototyping, fabrication, packaging, testing and industry-academia collaboration to bridge the gap between semiconductor design and product realisation.

Shri Sandeep Kumar, CEO, L&T Semiconductor Technologies, highlighted the architecture-led transformation of semiconductors through chiplets, Artificial Intelligence, high-speed interconnects and near-package optics, and stressed deeper capabilities in system architecture, power electronics, memory, optics and foundry supply chains.

A fireside discussion featuring Shri Ajit Manocha, President and CEO, SEMI, and Shri Mark Patel, Senior Partner, McKinsey & Company, examined the rapid expansion of the global semiconductor industry and India’s opportunity to build deeper capabilities in selected parts of the global value chain.

Ms. Nivruti Rai, MD and CEO, Invest India, highlighted the semiconductor industry’s evolution from the Integrated Device Manufacturer era to the foundry and fabless model and now towards an Artificial Intelligence and advanced-packaging-led era. She identified memory, High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), fabs, advanced packaging, materials, chiplets and heterogeneous integration as major opportunities for India, emphasising the need to combine India’s demand and engineering talent with global technology, capital and manufacturing expertise.

The session on Research and Development for Advanced Technologies, moderated by Ms. Sunita Verma, Scientist G and Group Coordinator, R&D Electronics, MeitY, emphasised indigenous R&D, intellectual property and commercialisation as critical to India’s next phase of semiconductor growth.

The State Spotlight session, moderated by Shri Vivek Tyagi, Managing Director, Analog Devices, highlighted initiatives of Assam, Odisha, Gujarat and Karnataka in incentives, infrastructure, ease of doing business and industry-linked skilling.

The Women in Manufacturing sessions highlighted expanding opportunities for women across semiconductor manufacturing, packaging, equipment engineering, quality, supply chains, automation and plant leadership, with emphasis on technical capability, mentorship and stronger pathways for women into leadership and decision-making roles.

The India Display Conference 2026 highlighted India’s opportunity to move beyond display assembly and build deeper domestic capabilities, with discussions covering advanced Liquid Crystal Displays (LCD), MiniLED, Quantum Dot and Organic Light-Emitting Diode (OLED) technologies, applications and supporting research.

The Workforce Development sessions focused on building an industry-ready talent pipeline across chip design, manufacturing, packaging, equipment, quality and supply chains through practical training and stronger industry–academia linkages.

India–Singapore Country Roundtable: Connecting Innovation and Investment

The India–Singapore Country Roundtable, attended by 142 participants representing both India and Singapore, explored cooperation by combining Singapore’s manufacturing, advanced packaging and supply-chain expertise with India’s engineering talent, market scale and expanding semiconductor ecosystem. Discussions covered equipment and materials, advanced packaging, R&D, testing, investment and talent, with emphasis on translating engagement into joint ventures and technology partnerships.

India–Europe Country Roundtable: Deepening Technology and Investment Partnerships

The India–Europe Country Roundtable, attended by 139 participants representing both India and Europe, focused on investment, supply-chain localisation, equipment and materials, manufacturing, advanced packaging, semiconductor design, R&D and talent. Discussions highlighted the complementarity between Europe’s capabilities in equipment, precision machinery, advanced materials and research and India’s strengths in design, engineering, manufacturing and market scale, including opportunities in 2.5D/3D packaging, chiplets and heterogeneous integration.

India–South Korea Country Roundtable: Strengthening Semiconductor Ecosystem Cooperation

The India–South Korea Country Roundtable, attended by 115 participants representing both India and South Korea, focused on opportunities to deepen cooperation across the semiconductor value chain, including manufacturing, technology, materials, advanced packaging, investment and supply chains, bringing together South Korea’s established semiconductor capabilities and India’s engineering talent, expanding market and growing manufacturing ecosystem.

Day 2 of SEMICON India 2026 reinforced India’s effort to build capabilities across the entire semiconductor value chain - from research, design and intellectual property to materials, equipment, fabs, advanced packaging, products and talent. The strong momentum was reflected in the participation of around 16,000 participants during the day, alongside extensive industry, research and international engagement. With growing investment, indigenous innovation and deeper global partnerships, India continues to strengthen its position as a trusted global partner for semiconductor design, manufacturing and innovation.

Vinod Kumar / Vineeth Narayan V / Vanshita Jaiswal / Kanishk Sharma

headline: CBIC and its field formations gear up for Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

CBIC and its field formations gear up for Special Campaign 6 from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026

Campaign to focus on cleanliness, disposal of pending matters and effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste

18 SEP 2026 9:44PM by PIB Delhi

The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), along with all its Zones, Directorates and field formations, is actively participating in Special Campaign 6, being conducted from 2nd October to 31st October, 2026, to institutionalise cleanliness and reduce pendency in Government offices. All formations have been sensitised to participate actively and to undertake the campaign in a focused and meaningful manner.

Special Campaign 6 builds on the successful efforts made by CBIC during Special Campaign 5.0. During the previous campaign, CBIC achieved 100 per cent of its targets in respect of identified cleanliness sites, references received from Members of Parliament, public grievances and public grievance appeals. The campaign also witnessed extensive action for review and weeding out of physical files, freeing up of office space and disposal of scrap.

During Special Campaign 5.0, 41,055 physical files were reviewed and 23,743 files were weeded out. The campaign also resulted in the freeing up of 43,009 square feet of office space and disposal of 22,728 kg of scrap, including 8,801 kg of e-waste in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. CBIC formations also undertook the safe destruction of approximately 250 kg of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances and about 26 lakh foreign-origin cigarettes and e-cigarettes and allied items.

Building on the momentum of Special Campaign 5.0, CBIC and all its Zones, Directorates and field formations are participating in Special Campaign 6 with full enthusiasm. In furtherance of the previous year's focus on scientific management of e-waste, this year's campaign will particularly emphasise “Effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste”, besides cleanliness, record management, space management and expeditious disposal of pending matters.

CBIC remains committed to sustaining the momentum generated through the Special Campaign and to making cleanliness, efficient record management and environmentally responsible disposal practice a continuing part of its administrative functioning.

headline: Department of Fisheries Reaffirms Commitment to Swachhata and Good Governance under Special Campaign 6.0
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

Department of Fisheries Reaffirms Commitment to Swachhata and Good Governance under Special Campaign 6.0

18 SEP 2026 9:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, along with its subordinate offices and autonomous bodies, will actively participate in Special Campaign 6.0 from 2nd to 31st October 2026. The campaign, being undertaken in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), aims to institutionalize Swachhata and promote efficient office management through reduction of pendency, improved record management, optimal utilization of office space, and systematic disposal of scrap and e-waste.

Building upon the significant achievements of Special Campaign 5.0 conducted in October 2025, the Department has resolved to further strengthen its cleanliness and administrative reforms initiatives during the current campaign.

Special Campaign 6.0 will be implemented in two phases, comprising a Preparatory Phase from 16th to 30th September 2026 and an Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31st October 2026.

As part of the preparatory activities, a hybrid review meeting was convened on 17th September 2026 by the Department's Nodal Officer with representatives of all subordinate offices and autonomous bodies. The meeting focused on finalization of action plans, target setting, conduct of cleanliness drives, reduction of pendency, strengthening of record management practices, and effective disposal of scrap and e-waste. Emphasis was also laid on robust monitoring and timely reporting to ensure successful implementation of the campaign across all offices.

Through its active participation in Special Campaign 6.0, the Department reaffirms its commitment to institutionalizing Swachhata, enhancing workplace efficiency, streamlining office processes, and fostering a clean, organized, and citizen-centric work environment.

headline: Indian Railways Approves ₹142 Crore for Upgradation of Electric Traction System to 2x25 kV on 73 RKM Savalyapuram-Guntur Section
fullText:
Ministry of Railways

Indian Railways Approves ₹142 Crore for Upgradation of Electric Traction System to 2x25 kV on 73 RKM Savalyapuram-Guntur Section

Upgradation Covering 146 TKM to Strengthen Traction Capacity and Enhance Operational Efficiency on Key South Coast Railway Section

19 SEP 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has approved the upgradation of the electric traction system from 1x25 kV to 2x25 kV on the 73 Route Kilometre Savalyapuram-Guntur section of South Coast Railway at a total cost of ₹142 crore. Covering 146 Track Kilometres, the project will strengthen the electric traction infrastructure and enhance its capacity to support growing railway operations.

The upgradation of the electric traction system on the Savalyapuram-Guntur section forms part of HUN Route 8, covering the Vasco-Gadag-Guntakal-Nandyal-Savalyapuram-Guntur-Vijayawada route.

The upgraded traction system will strengthen the power supply infrastructure for electric train operations on the Savalyapuram-Guntur section, enabling Indian Railways to cater to growing traffic requirements more efficiently. The intervention will also reinforce the capacity and reliability of this important HUN route, supporting smoother train operations and strengthening the overall rail network in the region.

This upgradation reflects Indian Railways’ continued focus on modernising traction infrastructure, enhancing network capacity and preparing the railway system for future traffic growth.

headline: Indian Railways Approves ₹133 Crore for Construction of Four-Lane Road Over Bridge on Udhna-Ukai Songadh Section of Western Railway
fullText:
Ministry of Railways

Indian Railways Approves ₹133 Crore for Construction of Four-Lane Road Over Bridge on Udhna-Ukai Songadh Section of Western Railway

Four-Lane ROB to Replace Level Crossing No. 53 at Km 62/2-4 on Cost-Sharing Basis with State Government

19 SEP 2026 3:23PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has approved the construction of a four-lane Road Over Bridge (ROB) in lieu of Level Crossing No. 53 at Km 62/2-4 on the Udhna-Ukai Songadh section of Western Railway, at a total cost of ₹133.2295 crore, on a cost-sharing basis with the State Government.

The ROB will be a four-lane structure. The Railway bridge portion will comprise an Open Web Girder (OWG), with an estimated cost of ₹91.60 crore.

The crossing location has a 62% skew, which significantly increases design and construction complexity.

The viaduct portion will have a total length of 311.58 metres, with an estimated cost of ₹19.98 crore. The Railway Approach (RE) portion will have a length of 524.32 metres, with an estimated cost of ₹10.25 crore.

The total cost of the work is ₹133.2295 crore, to be shared between Indian Railways and the State Government. The Railway share is ₹66.6147 crore, while the State Government share is ₹66.6148 crore.

The construction of the four-lane ROB will facilitate smoother movement of road traffic, thereby reducing interference with railway operations. The grade-separated infrastructure will support smoother train operations and contribute to safer and more efficient railway movement on the Udhna-Ukai Songadh section, benefiting passengers through improved operational efficiency and reliability.

Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj

headline: Rozgar Mela
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

12.75 Lakh+ Appointment Letters Distributed Across 20 Editions

19 SEP 2026 2:32PM by PIB Delhi

The National Rozgar Mela is a government initiative focused on accelerating recruitment to government posts while expanding employment opportunities for youth. Launched in October 2022 with an initial target of 10 lakh government jobs, the initiative has evolved into a nationwide mission-mode recruitment effort. The initiative has completed 20 editions and facilitated the distribution of 12.75 lakh appointment letters. The 20th edition distributed over 51,000 appointment letters in September 2026. The initiative brings together recruitment, skill development, career counselling and entrepreneurship support, connecting youth with diverse employment pathways. By facilitating direct interaction between job seekers and employers and supporting skill-to-job linkages, Rozgar Melas contribute to strengthening the skilled workforce and enabling young people to participate in public service and national development.

Rozgar Mela: Accelerating Government Recruitment

The 20th edition of the National Rozgar Mela was conducted on 19 September 2026, with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi addressing the event through video conferencing and distributing over 51,000 appointment letters to newly inducted youth in government departments and organisations.

The National Rozgar Mela is a government initiative focused on expediting recruitment to government posts and filling vacancies across Ministries, Departments and organisations. It is part of the Government’s broader focus on youth empowerment, timely recruitment and nation-building.

Launched on 22 October 2022, the initiative initially focused on facilitating the recruitment of 10 lakh individuals to government posts in a time-bound manner. The first Rozgar Mela distributed more than 75,000 appointment letters at 50 locations across the country. Through the first 19 editions, over 12 lakh recruitment letters have been issued, exceeding the original target.

Recruitment has been pursued through a mission-mode approach, with Ministries and Departments working to fill vacancies against sanctioned posts. The process is undertaken through established recruitment mechanisms and designated agencies such as the Union Public Service Commission, Staff Selection Commission, and Railway Recruitment Boards.

The new recruits have joined the Ministry of Railways, Ministry of Home Affairs, Department of Posts, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Labour and Employment, and many other departments.

The initiative has accelerated public recruitment while creating opportunities for young people to begin their careers in public service and contribute to the nation’s development.

Rozgar Mela: Connecting Youth with Employment Opportunities

A Rozgar Mela is a half-day event that brings employers and job seekers together to apply and interview for available employment opportunities. It facilitates direct interaction between employers and prospective candidates, enabling them to explore suitable job opportunities.

The National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) organises Rozgar Melas in collaboration with Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs). Private sector employers are mobilised to participate in these events and offer employment opportunities to eligible candidates.

Empower youth through access to employment and skill development opportunities

Facilitate direct interaction between job seekers and employers

Enable skilled youth to participate in the workforce and contribute to national development

Reflect the Prime Minister’s vision of equitable development across the country

Who Can Participate?

Rozgar Melas generally cater to youth aged 18 to 35 years and offer employment opportunities to candidates with diverse educational and skill backgrounds, including:

8th, 10th and 12th pass candidates

ITI and Diploma holders

Trained and certified candidates aligned with the National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)

Information about Rozgar Melas is disseminated through print advertisements, bulk SMS, and social media platforms. Workshops in colleges and universities, along with targeted outreach in and around the districts where the Melas are organised, further help connect eligible candidates with these employment opportunities.

Beyond Recruitment

Rozgar Melas also provide complementary services that support career planning, skill development and entrepreneurship, enabling participants to explore employment and livelihood pathways beyond immediate job opportunities.

Career Counselling

Sessions for job seekers and, where applicable, their parents to help them understand available employment opportunities and make informed career choices.

Youth can register for fresh skill development training under programmes such as Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendra (PMKK)-related training.

Mudra Loan Facilitation

Facilitation counters provide information and support on available credit opportunities for aspiring entrepreneurs. NSDC also has a formal linkage with the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) to facilitate access to credit for skilled candidates seeking to establish or expand enterprises.

Skill Exhibitions

Sector Skill Councils showcase training models, equipment, and job roles from their respective sectors, helping participants understand different occupations and available career pathways.

How Rozgar Melas Benefit Stakeholders

For Job Seekers: Direct interaction with employers and access to job and entrepreneurship opportunities.

For Employers: A common platform to meet potential employees and identify suitable candidates.

For the Skill Ecosystem: Connects candidates, recruiters, SSCs, and training providers.

20th | 19 September, 2026 | 51,000+ | 45 locations, With the 20th Rozgar Mela, a total of about 12.75 lakh youth have received appointment letters in various Departments and Government Organisations.

The Rozgar Mela provides a platform for direct interaction between job seekers and employers, helping address the challenge of unemployment while empowering youth to contribute to national development. With employment, skill development, counselling, and entrepreneurship opportunities brought together, Rozgar Melas continue to connect youth with opportunities and support the development of a skilled workforce. The 20th edition further strengthens this nationwide effort to expand access to employment opportunities.

* **First Edition**: The inaugural event on October 22, 2022, distributed over 75,000 appointment letters across 50 locations nationwide.
* **Participating Departments**: New recruits have joined various ministries and departments, including the Ministry of Railways, Ministry of Home Affairs, Department of Posts, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Department of Financial Services, and Ministry of Labour and Employment.
* **Target Demographic**: Caters to youth aged 18 to 35 years, welcoming candidates with diverse educational and skill backgrounds, including 8th, 10th, and 12th pass candidates, ITI and diploma holders, and NSQF-certified candidates.
* **Organizational Framework**: Organized by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) in collaboration with Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras (PMKKs), with active participation from private sector employers.
* **Complementary Support Services**: Beyond direct recruitment, the Melas provide career counselling, skill development training registration under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) or PMKK-related training, Mudra loan facilitation for entrepreneurs, and sector-specific skill exhibitions.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi distributes more than 51,000 appointment letters to the newly appointed youth in Government at 20th Rozgar Mela

India's Yuva Shakti is at the heart of our journey towards a Viksit Bharat.: PM

The Rozgar Mela reflects our commitment to creating new opportunities for the youth: PM

Our youth's talent and skills have earned global confidence; the world pins great hopes on our innovators, our entrepreneurs, and our vibrant youth force: PM

Free Trade Agreements are unlocking new avenues of opportunity for our youth; these trade agreements pave the way for new partnerships and markets for our entrepreneurs, while creating fresh career possibilities for our youth: PM

India is currently the world's third-largest startup ecosystem; Moreover, India's startup story is no longer confined to major metropolitan areas, today, roughly half of all recognized startups are based in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities: PM

19 SEP 2026 2:30PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi distributed more than 51,000 appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various government organizations at the 20th Rozgar Mela today via video conferencing. Addressing on the occasion, he emphasized that this milestone brings immense joy to thousands of families, serving as a tribute to both the personal hard work of the candidates and the immense sacrifices made by their parents. "I wish you all the very best for this new beginning in life,” remarked Shri Modi.

Welcoming the new appointees into the Government of India as the nation marches toward the monumental milestone of a developed nation by 2047, the Prime Minister emphasized the pivotal role of youth in continuously empowering the twin campaigns of a developed and self-reliant India through every administrative decision. He highlighted their special responsibility toward fellow youth, noting that the talent and skills of the younger generation have captured the world's trust, fueling immense global expectations from Indian innovators, entrepreneurs, and youth power."The world has high hopes from our innovators, our entrepreneurs, and our youth power,” asserted Shri Modi.

Reflecting on the recently concluded BRICS Summit, the Prime Minister stated that the administration’s strategy is to expand international cooperation far beyond traditional government-to-government interactions. He explained that initiatives like BRICS CONNECT and the BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal are designed to integrate entrepreneurs, farmers, women, and the youth directly into global partnerships. "Everyone should become an active participant in this partnership,” noted Shri Modi.

Highlighting the economic diplomacy of the past few years, the Prime Minister pointed out that Free Trade Agreements with approximately 40 countries are unlocking unprecedented career possibilities. He emphasized that these agreements forge new markets and dynamic partnerships for domestic entrepreneurs while expanding career horizons for the youth. "These Free Trade Agreements are creating new doors of possibilities for our youth,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Detailing the government's sustained focus on future-ready skilling, the Prime Minister listed transformative initiatives such as the National Education Policy, the Skill India Mission, the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, and efforts to promote apprenticeships. He highlighted the PM-SETU scheme, which is modernizing one thousand government ITIs with an investment of 60,000 crore rupees alongside direct industry participation. "Our endeavor is that the education and skills of the youth keep pace with the needs of the changing economy,” asserted Shri Modi.

Praising the explosive growth of the domestic startup ecosystem, the Prime Minister celebrated the nation's position as the world's third-largest startup hub, noting that nearly half of recognized startups now hail from tier-two and tier-three cities. He commended the youth from smaller towns for actively working on their ideas, building companies, and generating new employment opportunities for their peers. "Today the youth from villages, towns, and small cities are also playing a major role in India's new economy,” observed Shri Modi.

Outlining the strategy to boost private sector employment, the Prime Minister highlighted the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana, a massive one lakh crore rupee initiative aiming to introduce two crore youths into the formal workforce for the first time. He detailed that the scheme offers up to 15,000 rupees in incentives for first-time employees while also financially rewarding employers who generate new jobs. "The government is working on every front to increase employment in the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Connecting job creation to robust macroeconomic health, the Prime Minister explained that new youth opportunities emerge only when the economy grows, investments increase, and new industries expand. He highlighted the nation's impressive 7.8 percent growth rate and a 12 percent surge in investments during the first quarter, noting that rating agencies are upgrading the nation's economic outlook despite pervasive global uncertainties. "The reforms of the past years have a major contribution behind this growth of India,” noted Shri Modi.

Directing the new officials to embrace an era of continuous administrative transformation, the Prime Minister stressed the critical need to simplify tax compliance, enhance the ease of doing business, implement reforms in education and skilling, and open new sectors to innovation. He tasked the young bureaucrats with ensuring that the momentum of governance improvements remains unstoppable throughout their tenures. "It is necessary that the Reform Express in the country runs continuously at full speed,” asserted Shri Modi.

Invoking his poetic remarks about claiming the sun, the sea, the boat, and the sailor to conquer the waves, the Prime Minister challenged the new recruits to match this courage by championing the deep aspirations of the country's youth. He insisted that every file signature and every administrative decision must actively clear hurdles, allow ideas to flourish, and promote innovation-driven investment that ultimately creates employment. "Your signature on every file should be one that advances youth aspirations,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Appealing to their personal journeys, the Prime Minister urged the fresh appointees to utilize their new authority within the government system with deep empathy. He advised them to actively dismantle the bureaucratic hurdles they themselves faced before joining the service. "Your effort should be that the difficulties you have gone through, other youths should not have to go through them,” remarked Shri Modi.

Encouraging a mindset of lifelong learning in a rapidly changing world, the Prime Minister directed the recruits to continuously upgrade their skills and master new technologies through the Mission Karmayogi framework. He noted that the 'Karmayogi Prarambh' module has been specifically designed to help new entrants navigate the system, joining the 1.7 crore employees already on the iGOT platform. "The more you improve yourself, the better you will be able to serve the citizens of the country,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Emphasizing that the true strength of any government lies in public trust, the Prime Minister reminded the recruits that their daily work, from processing elderly pensions to student scholarships and farmer subsidies, directly impacts common lives. He stressed that their behavior, efficiency, honesty, and sensitivity will ultimately define the citizen's personal experience with the state. "Your behavior, your sensitivity, your efficiency, your honesty, all this will determine what that citizen's experience with the government is like,” observed Shri Modi.

Concluding his address with a powerful administrative mantra, the Prime Minister called upon the new officials to adopt the philosophy of 'Nagrik Devo Bhava' (The Citizen is Divine) in their daily service, equating citizen service to national service. He expressed his unwavering belief that they will fulfill their duties with utmost dedication and service across all departments. "Your success will be even greater when your work makes a citizen's life easier,” affirmed Shri Modi.

headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’ in New Delhi; Releases NGT Mobile Application
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’ in New Delhi; Releases NGT Mobile Application

Union Minister Shri Bhupender Yadav underscores India’s commitment to Climate Action anchored in Equity, Implementation and Sustainable Development

Two-day Conference brings together Global Stakeholders to deliberate on Collaborative Action on Pressing Global Environmental and Climate Challenges

19 SEP 2026 2:09PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the National Green Tribunal’s (NGT) two-day International Conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’, in New Delhi today. The inaugural session was graced by Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant, Attorney General for India Shri R. Venkataramani, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav and Chairperson, National Green Tribunal, Justice Prakash Shrivastava.

Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister highlighted the nation's profound historical connection to nature, emphasizing how ancient cultural wisdom is actively shaping modern climate solutions and inspiring global collective action. He commended the National Green Tribunal for steadfastly advancing this critical mission and extended his congratulations to the organizers. (Link: https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseDetail.aspx?PRID=2312353®=48&lang=1)

Delivering his inaugural remarks, Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant highlighted India’s longstanding environmental jurisprudence, noting that the Supreme Court has, over the decades, recognised the right to a pollution-free environment as a fundamental right and developed principles including the precautionary principle, polluter pays principle, absolute liability and public trust doctrine. The Chief Justice said Indian climate jurisprudence has brought climate-related rights into sharper constitutional focus, recognising that adverse effects of climate change can implicate fundamental rights relating to equality, livelihood and health. He called for collective judicial wisdom, scientific knowledge and international cooperation to strengthen global environmental stewardship.

Addressing the august gathering, Shri Bhupender Yadav highlighted India’s climate commitments under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, noting that non-fossil sources now account for 54.18 per cent of installed electricity capacity, surpassing the 2030 target of 50 per cent nine years ahead of schedule. He said India ranks third globally in renewable energy installed capacity and is the world’s second-largest solar growth market, demonstrating that economic growth and climate action can advance together.

Shri Yadav also highlighted India’s achievements in wildlife and ecosystem conservation, from the successful Cheetah reintroduction programme and conservation breeding programme of the Great Indian Bustard to the conservation and restoration of woodlands, grasslands and wetlands. He said India’s forest and tree cover has reached 8.27 lakh square kilometres and quoted the Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025 by the UN FAO, according to which India has retained its third position globally in terms of annual net forest-area gain. Looking ahead to UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, he said India will continue to advocate climate action centred on equity, implementation and the needs of vulnerable countries.

The Union Minister said that forums bringing together judges, policymakers, scientists, practitioners and experts from across the world are vital at a time when environmental challenges transcend national boundaries. He emphasised that the choice before the world is not between development and environment, but between sustainable development and development that cannot be sustained. The Minister said India’s approach to environmental responsibility is rooted in its civilisational ethos, which views the Earth as a shared inheritance and a sacred trust, and reaffirmed India’s commitment to collective action towards a sustainable, resilient and just future.

In his speech, Attorney General for India Shri R. Venkataramani said that no country can address the environmental challenge alone and that global action must move beyond declarations towards practical and enforceable mechanisms. Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call that “global action must match global ambitions”, he said India can set examples through the balancing path it has chosen while pursuing development and environmental protection. He called for a new global environmental regulatory framework and stronger international institutions to address environmental justice, while integrating concerns relating to energy and food security, housing, health, water, ecosystems and economic opportunities.

Welcoming the delegates earlier, NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava highlighted India’s comprehensive approach to environmental governance under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He said that India's initiatives demonstrate the country's commitment not only to national action but also to global environmental cooperation. Justice Shrivastava said the initiatives reflect a larger vision of a cleaner, greener, more resilient and sustainable India. He emphasised that environmental protection is not the responsibility of any one institution or sector, but a collective national and global responsibility, with the consequences of environmental degradation often falling most severely on those least responsible for them.

The Prime Minister also launched the National Green Tribunal (NGT) Mobile Application during the inaugural session of the conference.

The two-day Conference is bringing together jurists, academicians, policymakers, scientists, environmental experts and other stakeholders from 17 countries across the world, along with international organisations United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and Asian Development Bank (ADB). The event focuses on dialogue, knowledge exchange on judicial, scientific, policy and institutional best practices, while encouraging collaborative action on pressing environmental and climate challenges.

The Conference features four technical sessions covering key aspects of environmental and climate governance, two of which were held today.

Technical Session-I - ‘Climate Justice, Equity and Inclusion: From Principles to Action’ - focused on equity and inclusion in climate action, environmental and social safeguards, and the interconnected impacts of climate change and environmental degradation.

Technical Session-II - ‘The Future of Environmental Law and Governance’ - discussed strengthening institutions and enforcement mechanisms, sustainable and liveable cities, energy transition, green infrastructure and green finance.

The Conference seeks to strengthen environmental law and institutions, advance climate justice and inter-generational equity, promote sustainable and resilient cities, facilitate a just energy transition and foster collaborative action on transboundary environmental challenges. It also focused on sharing research, best practices and innovative solutions, building partnerships, and developing actionable recommendations and a roadmap for future cooperation.

headline: Text of PM’s remarks during 20th Rozgar Mela via video conferencing
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Text of PM’s remarks during 20th Rozgar Mela via video conferencing

19 SEP 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi

मेरे प्यारे युवा साथियों,

देश में त्योहारों का समय शुरू हो चुका है। इन खुशियों के बीच, आज का दिन हजारों परिवारों के जीवन में एक नई खुशी लेकर आया है। आज देश के 51 हजार से अधिक युवाओं को सरकारी सेवा के लिए नियुक्ति पत्र मिल रहे हैं। आज आप जिस मुकाम पर पहुंचे हैं, उसके पीछे आपकी मेहनत तो है ही, साथ ही,आपके माता-पिता और आपके परिवारजनों की भी तपस्या है। मैं आप सभी युवा साथियों को और आपके परिवारजनों को बहुत-बहुत बधाई देता हूं। जीवन की इस नई शुरुआत के लिए आप सभी को शुभकामनाएं देता हूं।

आज आप सभी एक ऐसे समय में भारत सरकार से जुड़े हैं, जब देश एक बहुत बड़े लक्ष्य की ओर आगे बढ़ रहा है, और ये लक्ष्य है- 2047 तक विकसित भारत बनाने का। इसमें आप जैसे युवाओं की बहुत बड़ी भूमिका है। सरकार में रहते हुए आपको हर वो निर्णय लेना है, जो विकसित भारत के अभियान को, आत्मनिर्भर भारत के अभियान को निरंतर सशक्त करे। युवा होने के नाते विशेषतौर पर अन्य युवाओं के प्रति आपकी विशेष जिम्मेदारी है। आज आप देख रहे हैं, हमारे युवाओं के टैलेंट और स्किल्स ने पूरी दुनिया का भरोसा जीता है। दुनिया को हमारे innovators, हमारे entrepreneurs और हमारी युवा शक्ति से बहुत उम्मीदें है। अभी कुछ दिन पहले ही ब्रिक्स समिट संपन्न हुई। भारत का प्रयास रहा है कि BRICS cooperation केवल सरकारों तक सीमित न रहे, हमारे entrepreneurs, हमारे किसान, हमारी महिलाएं, हमारे युवा, हर कोई इस partnership का सक्रिय भागीदार बने। इसी सोच के साथ BRICS CONNECT और BRICS MSME Cooperation Portal की भी पहल की गई है।

भारत ने बीते कुछ वर्षों में करीब 40 देशों के साथ फ्री ट्रेड एग्रीमेंट भी किए हैं। ये फ्री ट्रेड एग्रीमेंट्स, FTA, हमारे युवाओं के लिए संभावनाओं के नए द्वार बना रहे हैं। इस तरह के ट्रेड एग्रीमेंट्स से हमारे entrepreneurs के लिए नई partnerships के रास्ते खुलते हैं, नए markets के रास्ते खुलते हैं। और हमारे युवाओं के लिए करियर में नई possibilities बनती हैं।

बीते वर्षों में भारत सरकार का निरंतर जोर युवाओं को भविष्य के लिए तैयार करने पर रहा है। National Education Policy, Skill India Mission, प्रधानमंत्री कौशल विकास योजना या अप्रेंटिसशिप को बढ़ावा देने के प्रयास। हमारी कोशिश है कि युवाओं की पढ़ाई और उनकी skills, बदलती economy की जरूरतों के साथ चलें। जैसे एक उदाहरण है, PM-SETU। इस योजना के माध्यम से 60 हजार करोड़ रुपए के निवेश से एक हजार सरकारी ITIs को आधुनिक बनाया जा रहा है। इसमें इंडस्ट्री की सीधी भागीदारी सुनिश्चित की गई है।

भारत के युवाओं के सामर्थ्य की एक और तस्वीर हमारे startup ecosystem में दिखाई देती है। भारत आज दुनिया का तीसरा सबसे बड़ा startup ecosystem है। और भारत की startup story अब केवल बड़े शहरों की कहानी नहीं है। आज करीब आधे recognised startups टीयर-टू और टीयर-थ्री शहरों में हैं। यानी आज गांव, कस्बे और छोटे शहर का युवा भी भारत की नई economy में अपनी भूमिका बड़ी बना रहा है। छोटे शहरों के हमारे युवा अपने ideas पर काम कर रहे हैं, नई companies बना रहे हैं, और अपने साथ दूसरे युवाओं के लिए भी रोजगार के नए अवसर तैयार कर रहे हैं।

हमारा प्रयास है कि private sector में भी रोजगार के नए अवसर तेजी से बढ़ें। इसी सोच के साथ प्रधानमंत्री विकसित भारत रोजगार योजना शुरू की गई है। इस योजना पर करीब एक लाख करोड़ रुपए खर्च किए जा रहे हैं। इस योजना की मदद से करीब दो करोड़ युवाओं को पहली बार workforce का हिस्सा बनने का मौका मिलेगा। सरकार द्वारा इस योजना के तहत पहली बार नौकरी पाने वाले युवाओं को15 हजार रुपए तक का incentive भी दिया जा रहा है। नए रोजगार पैदा करने वाले employers को भी सरकार प्रोत्साहन दे रही है। यानि देश में रोजगार बढ़ाने के लिए सरकार हर मोर्चे पर काम कर रही है।

युवाओं के लिए नए अवसर तभी बनते हैं, जब देश की इकोनॉमी आगे बढ़ती है, जब investment बढ़ता है, नए उद्योग लगते हैं, और नए सेक्टर्स का विस्तार होता है। आज भारत तेजी से ग्रो करने वाली बड़ी अर्थव्यवस्था है। इस financial year की पहली तिमाही में भारत की growth rate 7.8 प्रतिशत रही है। Investment में करीब 12 प्रतिशत की बढ़ोतरी हुई है। रेटिंग एजेंसियां, भारत की रेटिंग्स सुधार रही हैं। और ये प्रगति ऐसे समय में हो रही है, जब दुनिया अनेक अनिश्चितताओं से गुजर रही है। भारत की इस growth के पीछे बीते वर्षों के reforms का बड़ा योगदान है। आपको अपने कार्यकाल में निरंतर reforms को और गति देनी है। Tax और compliance को सरल बनाना हो, ईज ऑफ डूइंग बिजनेस को बढ़ाना हो, एजुकेशन और स्किलिंग में reform हों, या नए सेक्टर्स को इनोवेशन के लिए खोलना हो या ईज ऑफ लिविंग की बात हो, हर स्तर पर देश में Reform Express का लगातार फुल स्पीड में चलना जरूरी है। और सरकारी कर्मचारी होने के नाते वर्तमान और आने वाले वर्षों में इसमें आप सभी की बहुत बड़ी भूमिका रहेगी।

मैंने कुछ दिन पहले कहा था, सूरज हमारा हो, समंदर भी हमारा हो। सूरज हमारा हो, समंदर भी हमारा हो। नाव हमारी हो, नाव हमारी हो, नाविक भी हमारा हो। लहरों पर विजय लिखें, लहरों पर विजय लिखें, वो हौसला हमारा हो। आज भारत का युवा इसी हौसले के साथ आगे बढ़ रहा है। अब आप सभी की भारत सरकार में रहते हुए ये जिम्मेदारी है कि देश के युवाओं की आकांक्षाओं को समझते हुए आप अपने काम को बखूबी निभाएं। मेरा फिर आग्रह होगा, आपका हर निर्णय, हर फाइल पर किया गया सिग्नेचर, युवा Aspirations को आगे बढ़ाने वाला होना चाहिए। आपको अपने कार्यकाल में देखना होगा, युवाओं के रास्ते की बाधाएं हटें, उनके ideas को आगे बढ़ाने का अवसर मिले, innovation से investment बढ़े और investment से employment के नए अवसर बनें।

अब आप स्वयं सरकारी व्यवस्था का हिस्सा बनने जा रहे हैं। इसलिए आपका प्रयास हो कि जिन परेशानियों से आप गुजरे हैं या जिन परेशानियों से आपके माता-पिता को गुजरना पड़ा है, उनसे दूसरे युवाओं को न गुजरना पड़े। जो तकलीफें आपके मां-बाप ने सही है, जो तकलीफें कभी आपको सहनी पड़ी हैं, वो अब हमारे देश के किसी नागरिक को सहनी ना पड़े, ये काम आपको सरकारी व्यवस्था में आते ही करना चाहिए।

आज देश में, हर क्षेत्र में तेजी से परिवर्तन हो रहा है। आप लगातार सीखते हुए, यहां तक पहुंचे हैं, अब यहां से निरंतर सीखते रहने की एक नई यात्रा शुरू हो रही है। आपको लगातार अपनी skills को बेहतर करना है। नई Technology और नए systems को समझना है। मिशन कर्मयोगी इसी उद्देश्य को पूरा करने में आपकी मदद करता है। iGOT Karmayogi Platform पर आज एक करोड़ 70 लाख से अधिक सरकारी कर्मचारी जुड़ चुके हैं। और आप जैसे नए साथियों के लिए कर्मयोगी प्रारंभ को विशेष रूप से तैयार किया गया है। आप जितना खुद को बेहतर बनाएंगे, उतना ही बेहतर देश के नागरिकों की सेवा कर पाएंगे।

आपको एक और बात हमेशा याद रखनी है। सरकार की असली ताकत देश के नागरिकों का विश्वास होता है। आप किसी भी मंत्रालय में हों, किसी भी विभाग में हों, आपका काम किसी न किसी रूप में देश के सामान्य नागरिक के जीवन को छुएगा। किसी बुजुर्ग की पेंशन आपके काम से आगे बढ़ेगी। किसी विद्यार्थी की स्कॉलरशिप आपकी जिम्मेदारी से जुड़ी होगी। किसी किसान को मिलने वाली सुविधा आपके डिपार्टमेंट में से हो जाती होगी। हो सकता है, किसी नागरिक के लिए आप ही सरकार का चेहरा हो। आपका व्यवहार, आपकी संवेदनशीलता, आपकी efficiency, आपकी ईमानदारी, इन सबसे तय होगा कि उस नागरिक का सरकार के साथ अनुभव कैसा रहता है।

सरकारी सेवा में हमारा मंत्र होना चाहिए- नागरिक देवो भव, नागरिक देवो भव। नागरिक की सेवा, राष्ट्र की सेवा है। आपकी सफलता तब और बड़ी होगी, जब आपके काम से किसी नागरिक का जीवन आसान होगा। मुझे विश्वास है, आप जहां भी रहेंगे, जिस भी विभाग में रहेंगे, कर्तव्य और सेवा भाव से अपने दायित्व को निभाते रहेंगे। मैं एक बार फिर आप सभी को बधाई देता हूं।

fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”

India is showing how development and environmental sustainability can go hand in hand: PM

Often, the responsibility for carbon emissions has been unfairly placed on developing countries; However, the historical truth is that even today, India's contribution to per capita carbon emissions is less than half of the global average: PM

Over the past 12 years, India has made extraordinary progress in every field and sector related to the environment; Our major focus has been on renewable energy, which has played a significant role in environmental protection: PM

Among the G-20, India is the only country to have met the commitments made at the COP-21 Summit in Paris ahead of time: PM

Our development is both speedy and sustainable: PM

19 SEP 2026 1:51PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics” today at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion, the Prime Minister highlighted the nation's profound historical connection to nature, emphasizing how ancient cultural wisdom is actively shaping modern climate solutions and inspiring global collective action. He commended the National Green Tribunal for steadfastly advancing this critical mission and extended his congratulations to the organizers. “India is now providing solutions to modern climate challenges,” asserted Shri Modi.

Addressing the flawed global narrative regarding carbon footprints, the Prime Minister pointed out that developing nations are unjustly blamed, despite developed nations emitting up to six times more carbon per capita than India. He detailed how the nation uses international platforms to assert this historical truth and showcase its traditional environmental strengths, recalling the launch of the "Convenient Action- Continuity for Change" book at COP-21 and the creation of platforms like One Sun, One World, One Grid, the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, the Global Biofuel Alliance, and the International Big Cat Alliance. "We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Bridging ancient philosophy with modern execution, the Prime Minister detailed the extraordinary progress made across every environmental sector over the past dozen years, specifically highlighting a massive strategic pivot toward renewable energy. He proudly stated that the nation proudly occupies a unique position within the G-20 for having achieved its COP-21 commitments ahead of schedule, setting global benchmarks in non-fossil fuels and solar capacity. "India's performance on every parameter is a topic of discussion in the world today,” noted Shri Modi.

Presenting stark evidence of the nation's solar revolution, the Prime Minister cited the leap from a mere 2 gigawatts of capacity a dozen years ago to over 160 gigawatts today, fueled by the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana which has solarized over 50 lakh homes with financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. He added that 30 lakh farmers have received solar pumps under the Kusum Yojana, while the completed One Nation-One Grid project has successfully prevented 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions. "We have started a mission to make homes themselves the center of solar power generation,” asserted Shri Modi.

Expanding on the massive strides in the broader clean energy landscape, the Prime Minister highlighted the threefold increase in wind capacity, significant hydro expansions, and a newly energized focus on nuclear power generation that now welcomes private players. He noted that these combined efforts have nearly quadrupled the nation's non-fossil energy capacity while advancing cleaner technologies like Coal Gasification. "India has achieved major milestones in other sectors of clean energy as well,” noted Shri Modi.

Celebrating the dawn of advanced clean mobility, the Prime Minister proudly announced the recent launch of the country's first Hydrogen Train, which also holds the record as the world's longest. He described this technological leap as a foundational milestone for the future of green transportation. "This is the beginning of a new era of clean mobility,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Detailing the massive adoption of green vehicles, the Prime Minister highlighted a staggering 950-fold increase in Electric Vehicles, jumping from under three thousand sales before 2014 to roughly 25 lakh last year. He also pointed out that the modern FASTag system on highways and expressways has drastically reduced fuel wastage by minimizing wait times at toll booths. "India is embracing this opportunity of the EV revolution with full force,” noted Shri Modi.

Showcasing the sweeping modernization of public transport infrastructure, the Prime Minister contrasted the meager five-city, 250-kilometer metro network of 2014 with today's expansive system operating in over 20 cities. "India has joined the ranks of those countries in the world that have a metro network of more than a thousand kilometers,” asserted Shri Modi.

Underscoring the eco-friendly transformation of heavy logistics, the Prime Minister explained how the near-total electrification of the railways has saved crores of liters of diesel from being burned. He highlighted the massive environmental benefits of the newly inaugurated 3,000-kilometer Dedicated Freight Corridor, where historic double-stack container trains are replacing hundreds of polluting trucks per journey. "You can imagine on what a large scale this is helping the environment,” observed Shri Modi.

Pointing to alternative eco-friendly transport modes, the Prime Minister celebrated the operationalization of approximately 5,000 kilometers of inland waterways across the country. He explained that a single standard inland vessel navigating these routes can carry a load equivalent to dozens of trucks. "This too is providing great help in environmental conservation,” noted Shri Modi.

Summarizing the collective impact of these transit upgrades, the Prime Minister emphasized that the sweeping changes across the entire mobility sector serve as undeniable proof of the nation's balanced growth trajectory. He stated that rapid progress is entirely compatible with environmental preservation. "Our development is speedy as well as sustainable,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Praising the unprecedented mass participation in water conservation, the Prime Minister celebrated the construction of over 70,000 Amrit Sarovars and 1.5 crore rainwater harvesting structures under the Catch the Rain campaign. He noted that modern irrigation techniques under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana and 'Per Drop, More Crop' are actively saving water for over 2 crore farmers. "Unprecedented work is being done on water conservation in India,” noted Shri Modi.

Championing the global revival of millets, the Prime Minister explained how promoting the cultivation of water-efficient Shree Anna has boosted domestic production and increased exports to 1.5 lakh tons, simultaneously creating economic opportunities and conserving water. He credited these relentless national efforts for inspiring the global celebration of 2023 as the International Year of Millets. "Because of this model, the world is also joining us,” remarked Shri Modi.'

Underscoring the massive scale of ecological agriculture, the Prime Minister detailed the establishment of 24,000 natural farming clusters across 12.5 lakh hectares under the National Mission on Natural Farming. He also highlighted the successful development of 3,000 climate-resilient crop varieties and the strategic promotion of agro-forestry to reduce the national footprint. "By promoting agro-forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints,” asserted Shri Modi.

Illustrating the comprehensive nature of the country's environmental efforts, the Prime Minister shared that the very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent over the last 12 years. He praised the ongoing 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign for inspiring citizens to plant crores of trees in a continuous, nationwide drive.

Addressing the critical challenge of plastic pollution, the Prime Minister reiterated the national ban on single-use plastics and the strong push toward a Circular Economy based on reducing, reusing, and recycling thousands of tons of daily waste. He cited the Gobardhan Yojana as a prime example of converting rural organic waste into valuable resources through a Wealth from Waste model. "Our endeavor is that instead of treating waste as a problem, it should be transformed into a resource,” affirmed Shri Modi.

Elevating the significance of the nation's environmental achievements, the Prime Minister stated that these robust statistics represent far more than domestic progress. He framed the nation's developmental data as monumental, direct contributions to the survival and prosperity of the entire human race. "These are also figures of India's contribution to the future of humanity,” asserted Shri Modi.

The Prime Minister underscored the profound relationship between the earth and its inhabitants that drives these responsible actions. He concluded his address on an optimistic note, expressing deep confidence that the conference deliberations would yield innovative solutions, and offered his final felicitations. "India is also working to build a responsible and sustainable future,” affirmed Shri Modi.

headline: English rendering of PM’s address at the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

English rendering of PM’s address at the International Conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”

19 SEP 2026 1:09PM by PIB Delhi

Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant ji, my colleague in the Union Cabinet Bhupender Yadav ji, Attorney General of India R. Venkataramani ji, National Green Tribunal (NGT) Chairman Justice Prakash Srivastava ji, all distinguished dignitaries present in this hall, ladies and gentlemen.

For centuries, India has guided the world on the subject of nature and environment. With that ideological commitment, and based on our cultural experiences, India is now also providing solutions to modern climate challenges, while at the same time calling for collective efforts of humanity. I am happy that this NGT conference is carrying forward that mission. For this event, I extend my congratulations and best wishes to all the officials of NGT and all dignitaries associated with it.

We all know that often the responsibility for carbon emissions has been wrongly placed on developing countries. Many of my companions from the Global South are present here. But the historical truth is that even today, India’s per capita carbon emissions are less than half the global average. In developed countries, per capita carbon emissions are six times higher than India’s. Six times higher. India presents this fact strongly on global platforms. And I say to every Indian - show your strength too. We have also presented our traditions and their power before the world. On these very subjects, during COP‑21 in Paris, we launched the book Convenient Action – Continuity for Change. We are establishing new benchmarks for environmental protection by taking the world along. Whether it is the vision of One Sun, One World, One Grid, or the International Solar Alliance, CDRI, Global Biofuel Alliance, International Big Cat Alliance, Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) - each of these platforms is becoming a stage for India’s dedicated commitments on climate and environment.

Today’s India is moving forward by weaving its ancient ideas of environmental protection into a modern vision. In the past 12 years, India has made extraordinary progress in every sector related to the environment. Our major focus has been on renewable energy, and this has played a big role in environmental protection. India is the only country in the G20 - I say this before the big leaders of the G20 - the only country that has fulfilled all the commitments it made at the COP‑21 summit in Paris, and has done so ahead of schedule. This is the strength of Hindustan that I am talking about. On every parameter - non‑fossil fuel, solar energy capacity, curbing carbon emissions - India’s performance is today a subject of positive discussion worldwide. Look at the figures. Twelve years ago, India’s solar energy capacity was about 2 gigawatts. Twelve years ago - 2 gigawatts. If there are lawyers here, please note these figures, they may come in handy. Today it has crossed 160 gigawatts. From 2 gigawatts to 160 gigawatts in 12 years. Under the PM Surya Ghar Free Electricity Scheme, we launched the mission to make homes themselves centers of solar power generation. Under this scheme, more than 5 million homes have already installed rooftop solar panels. This is more than the total number of homes in many countries. For this, the government has provided financial assistance of up to 80,000 rupees per household. Under the KUSUM scheme, the government has installed solar pumps in the fields of 3 million farmers. We have also completed the ambitious One Nation, One Grid project. Not only this - LED bulbs in homes have proven successful in saving electricity. Crores of LED bulbs have been distributed to households. And the results of these efforts are before us today. From solar energy alone, India has succeeded in preventing nearly 200 million tonnes of carbon emissions.

Along with solar energy, India has also achieved major accomplishments in other clean energy sectors. In the past 12 years, the country’s wind energy capacity has tripled. Hydropower capacity has increased significantly. And now the country is working rapidly on nuclear energy generation. Those who give long speeches on the environment - when I advance nuclear energy work, they will stand in the courts to stop it. A pathway has also been created to bring private players into this sector. Because of these efforts, today India’s non‑fossil energy capacity has nearly quadrupled. India is also promoting technologies like coal gasification for cleaner use of coal.

India is now working rapidly in areas like clean mobility and green hydrogen. Just a few days ago, India’s first hydrogen train was launched - and it is the world’s longest hydrogen train. This marks the beginning of a new era of clean mobility.

In 12 years, the number of electric vehicles in our country has increased nearly 950 times. 950 times. In the year before 2014, fewer than 3,000 EVs were sold in India. Last year, nearly 2.5 million EVs were sold in India. That means India is embracing the opportunity of the EV revolution with full strength, and this is also helping the environment. On our highways and expressways, modern fast‑track systems have reduced waiting at toll booths. This has stopped the fuel wastage that used to occur at toll booths.

Until 2014, in five cities of our country there was less than 250 kilometers of metro network. Lawyers here should note this figure. Before 2014, only five cities had less than 250 kilometers. Today, metros run in more than 20 cities, and India has joined the countries with more than 1,000 kilometers of metro network.

With nearly 100 percent electrification of railways, billions of liters of diesel burning has been avoided. The environment has been protected. Just this month, a 3,000‑kilometer‑long Dedicated Freight Corridor was inaugurated. Every train running on it carries loads equal to hundreds of trucks from one place to another. The operation of double‑stack container freight trains is historic in itself. You can imagine how greatly this helps the environment.

Today, transportation is happening on about 5,000 kilometers of waterways in the country. This is the most environment‑friendly mobility. A standard inland vessel running on these waterways carries loads equal to dozens of trucks in one journey. This too is greatly helping environmental protection.

All these changes in the mobility sector alone are proof that our development is both speedy and sustainable.

Today, with the participation of millions of people, unprecedented work is happening in India on water conservation. I am happy that more than 70,000 Amrit Sarovars have been constructed in the country. Under the Catch the Rain campaign, nearly 15 million water harvesting structures have been built, preserving rainwater. Through the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana, more than 20 million farmers today are connected with modern irrigation facilities. Initiatives like Per Drop More Crop are also saving water. Shri Anna - that is, millets - are another great successful example. India is promoting the cultivation of millets, which consume less water. In recent years, millet production has increased in the country, and exports have risen to about 150,000 tonnes. This is creating new opportunities for farmers, while also saving water. And because of this model, the world is joining us. Thanks to India’s efforts, 2023 was celebrated as the International Year of Millets.

Under the National Mission on Natural Farming, today about 1.25 million hectares in the country have developed 24,000 clusters of natural farming. Not only this, nearly 3,000 varieties of climate‑resilient crops have also been developed in the country. By promoting agro‑forestry, we are also reducing carbon footprints.

How wide‑ranging our efforts are can be seen in India’s forest coverage. This too I mention for my lawyer friends. In the past 12 years, our very dense forest cover has increased by more than 22 percent. This is a very big achievement. Under the campaign Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam (One Tree in the Name of Mother), crores of trees have been planted across the country. And this campaign continues.

Plastic waste has also been a major challenge for the environment. That is why India has banned single‑use plastic. With the mantra of reduce, reuse, and recycle, we have promoted the circular economy. Today, thousands of tonnes of waste are being recycled every day in India. Through the Gobardhan Yojana, cow dung and other organic waste in villages are being converted into useful resources. Our effort is that waste should not be seen as a problem, but transformed into a resource under the Waste to Wealth model.

All these figures are not just India’s development statistics - they are India’s contributions for the future of humanity.

Our cultural thought is - “Mata bhumih, putro aham prithivyah” - meaning, this earth is our mother and we are her children. With this thinking, India is working to build a responsible and sustainable future. I am confident that the discussions in this conference, and the new ideas and solutions that emerge from it, may become a great support for future generations. Once again, I extend my many best wishes to all of you for this conference. Thank you very much.

19 SEP 2026 10:54AM by PIB Delhi

The 21st Meeting of the Board of Directors of National Land Monetization Corporation Limited (NLMC) was held on 18 September 2026, to review the Corporation’s ongoing asset monetisation programme, financial performance and key institutional initiatives.

A major highlight of the meeting was the consideration and recommendation of monetisation proposals involving assets valued at over ₹5,000 crore. The proposals cover surplus land and building assets identified for monetisation and represent a significant step towards advancing the Government’s objective of unlocking the value of underutilised and surplus assets.

The Board reviewed the progress made by NLMC in facilitating the monetisation of surplus assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and other Government entities. The Corporation has been working closely with asset-owning entities to identify suitable assets, undertake necessary due diligence, facilitate valuation and structure appropriate monetisation processes, with an emphasis on transparency, efficiency and value realisation.

The Board was apprised of the pace and progress of asset monetisation undertaken by NLMC, including the initiatives being pursued across various asset-owning entities. The discussions focused on expediting the monetisation process, addressing implementation-related requirements and ensuring that identified assets move forward through appropriate and transparent mechanisms.

Appreciating the progress the Board also emphasised the importance of maintaining momentum and strengthening coordination with stakeholder entities to facilitate timely monetisation of surplus assets.

The Board further approved the Annual Financial Statements and Directors’ Report of NLMC for the financial year 2025–26.

The meeting also provided an opportunity to review NLMC’s ongoing initiatives aimed at strengthening its institutional and operational capabilities and creating a more structured framework for asset

The recommendation by the Board of proposals involving assets worth over ₹5,000 crore underscores the growing scale of NLMC’s engagement in the Government’s asset monetisation programme. By facilitating the productive use of surplus land and building assets, NLMC seeks to contribute to unlocking value from assets that may otherwise remain underutilised, while supporting asset-owning entities in pursuing transparent and commercially appropriate monetisation opportunities.

The Board reiterated NLMC’s continued focus on efficient, transparent and value-oriented monetisation of surplus assets, in alignment with the Government of India’s broader asset monetisation objectives. The Corporation will continue to work with concerned Ministries, Departments, CPSEs and other Government entities to facilitate the identification and monetisation of surplus assets and support the effective utilisation of public resources.

National Land Monetization Corporation Limited (NLMC) is a wholly owned Government of India company under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE), Ministry of Finance. NLMC works with asset-owning entities to facilitate the identification, assessment and monetisation of surplus assets through appropriate and transparent mechanisms. Its mandate is aimed at unlocking the value of surplus public assets and supporting the Government’s broader asset monetisation objectives.

headline: Ministry of Rural Development to Commence DDU-GKY 2.0 Training Batches Across Most States/UTs from October 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Rural Development

Ministry of Rural Development to Commence DDU-GKY 2.0 Training Batches Across Most States/UTs from October 2026

34,920 Rural Youth to Begin Skill Training Under DDU-GKY 2.0 in October 2026

19 SEP 2026 9:49AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Rural Development is set to roll out Deen Dayal Upadhyaya- Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) 2.0 training batches across most States/UTs from October 2026. Preparedness for the commencement of training batches was reviewed with 14 States/UTs in the first phase — Odisha, Mizoram, Sikkim, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, West Bengal, Himachal Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Puducherry, Karnataka, Telangana and Bihar.

1,164 batches with 34,920 rural youth will start their training in October 2026, against a sanctioned target of 3,57,112 rural youth to be trained by 31st December 2027 in these 14 States/UTs. As per the DDU-GKY 2.0 portal, allocation of 5.6 lakh targets towards more than 1,200 projects has been done by 24 States/UTs. Other States are in the advanced stages of target allocation. Review meetings in phases will expedite the processes of batch commencement.

Preparedness for DDU-GKY 2.0

DDU-GKY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for poor rural youth providing placement linked skill training. Duration of the training varies from 3 months to 12 months. The meeting reviewed the preparedness of States/UTs for implementation of DDU-GKY 2.0. The targets have been allocated to all the 31 participating States/UTs for 2-year period 2026-28. The Ministry emphasised that this is a crucial phase for State/UT action and called upon implementing States/UTs to accelerate the allocation of targets to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) and to commence batches as per envisaged timelines.

States/UTs are supposed to ensure allocation of targets to PIAs for commencement of training latest by 31 October 2026. States/UTs are at different stages of preparation, and, based on information received by this Ministry from across the implementing 31 States/UTs, more than 5 lakh targets have already been allocated to PIAs for mobilisation of eligible rural youths. Most of the States will be able to commence mobilization and training in the month of October, 2026.

Integrated DDU-GKY 2.0 Portal

The Ministry highlighted that the DDU-GKY 2.0 Integrated Portal is equipped to facilitate end-to-end project life cycle, promoting greater efficiency, transparency and digital monitoring.

The integration of the portal with State Treasury Portals, wherever pending, was reviewed. States/UTs were advised to complete the required integration by 30 September 2026 to facilitate online payments through the Grameen Kaushal Portal.

To familiarise PIAs with the end-to-end digital platform, the Ministry is organising regional workshops in hybrid mode at four locations during October 2026. States/UTs have been requested to ensure physical participation of a few PIAs in these workshops. The workshops are going to be held at Shillong (5.10.2026), Vijayavada (7.10.2026), Mumbai (9.10.2026) and Dharamshala (16.10.2026) providing opportunities to brief PIAs on the DDU-GKY 2.0 portal, its processes and functionalities, and to address implementation-related concerns.

The financial status of the scheme was also reviewed during the meeting. States/UTs participating in the review indicated that expenditure is expected to increase with the commencement of training batches from October 2026 onwards.

The review meeting was held with participation of Joint Secretary Skills and Director (Skills) and CEOs, COOs and other State officials over Video Conferencing.

headline: Unemployment Rate Reduced from 6% to 3.2% Due to Government’s Flagship Schemes: Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan
fullText:

Unemployment Rate Reduced from 6% to 3.2% Due to Government’s Flagship Schemes: Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan

Union Minister of State Dr. L. Murugan Distributes Appointment Letters to 285 Newly Recruited Candidates at 20th Rozgar Mela in Chennai

19 SEP 2026 8:02PM by PIB Chennai

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi participated through video conferencing in the 20th Rozgar Mela, organised at 45 locations across the country, and distributed appointment letters to more than 51,000 newly recruited youth.

Union Minister of State for Information & Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, participated in the Rozgar Mela held at D.G. Vaishnav College, Chennai. He distributed appointment letters to 285 newly recruited candidates selected for various Central Government Ministries, Departments, and organisations, extending his best wishes to youngsters joining key bodies including the Income Tax Department, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation (ESIC), Airports Authority of India, Ministry of Defence, Department of Posts, Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER), and Southern Railway.

Speaking at the event, Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan said that the newly recruited youth entering Government service would play an important role in achieving the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. He urged the recruits to view their responsibilities not merely as securing employment, but as an opportunity to serve the nation and contribute to its holistic development.

He stated that an appointment letter is not merely an order of appointment but an opportunity to serve the nation, noting that Government employees function as representatives and the face of the Government while interacting with citizens. He emphasised that honesty, accountability, empathy, and a humane approach towards the public should remain integral to public service.

The Union Minister highlighted that various flagship initiatives of the Government, including Make in India, Start-up India, Stand-up India, and the MUDRA loan scheme, have enabled the youth to emerge as job creators in addition to being job seekers. He stated that the unemployment rate has declined from 6 per cent to 3.2 per cent as a result of various initiatives undertaken by the Government.

Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan pointed out that the number of startups in the country, which stood at around 400 in 2014, has increased to more than 2.5 lakh, noting that a significant number of startup founders are youth below the age of 30.

He also underscored the importance of continuous learning, adoption of new technologies, and regular upgradation of professional skills. He highlighted the growing opportunities for youth in frontier sectors such as space technology and atomic energy, while noting the increasing participation of women across sectors, including space, defence, education, governance, and public administration.

The Union Minister added that more than 12.75 lakh appointment letters have been distributed through Rozgar Melas so far, reflecting the Government’s dedicated emphasis on creating employment opportunities for the youth.

Later, addressing the media, Union Minister Dr. L. Murugan said that Navodaya schools in Tamil Nadu would provide underprivileged and economically weaker students access to quality education, facilitate primary education in their mother tongue, and provide opportunities for students to learn various Indian languages.

The event was attended by Shri Sunil Bajpai, Principal Chief Commissioner of Income Tax, Tamil Nadu & Puducherry, along with other senior officials, recruits, and their families.
