Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh to Bring Together Youth Across 1000+ Locations on 20 September

497 MY Bharat Offices and Partner Organisations at 596 locations to Participate in Nationwide Youth Mobilisation

19 SEP 2026 7:59PM by PIB Delhi

The Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat – 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan will witness a major nationwide youth mobilisation on 20 September 2026, with the Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh being organised across 1,067 locations through MY Bharat and its partner organisations across the country.

The programme will be organised across 471 District MY Bharat Offices, along with 596 locations of partner organisations, bringing together youth through a collective Nasha Mukt Pledge and Signature Campaign. The extensive network of participating organisations includes educational and university bodies, industry associations, spiritual organisations, NGOs and local partner organisations.

Among the participating partner organisations are spiritual organisations including Maa Amritanandmayi Math conducting in 130 locations, Heartfulness in 74 locations and BAPS in 56 locations. The partner network also includes EPSI, CIPU, AIU , Project Point , ASSOCHAM , CII , FICCI , 245 local partner organisations and 18 MY Bharat chapters in private/premier institutes.

The Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh will bring the campaign’s message directly to young people through Nasha Mukt Pledge, Signature Campaign, thematic street plays, slogan writing and youth-led discussions. The participatory formats are aimed at creating spaces for young people to express their views, engage with peers and communities, and translate awareness into positive action.

The mobilisation follows the nationwide activities undertaken on 18 September, which marked the opening of the campaign’s current phase. The first day recorded participation across 259 institutions, with 1,430 activities conducted and 1,46,520 participants mobilised across all 28 States and 8 Union Territories. Activities included pledge-taking ceremonies, signature campaigns, thematic street plays and youth-led discussions.

The 100 Weeks Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan is being implemented as a sustained youth movement with a focus on prevention, awareness, healthy lifestyles and positive youth engagement. The first activity cycle is structured around three broad themes—My Health, My Pride; Fit Youth, Addiction-Free Youth; and Life Skills Month—with activities designed to promote health, fitness, community participation and life skills.

The Rashtriya Sankalp Samaroh on 20 September will therefore serve as a significant nationwide moment of youth participation, bringing together MY Bharat, partner organisations and young people around a shared commitment to healthier choices and a Nasha Mukt future.

headline: Biometric Aadhaar Authentication Mandatory for Subsidised Domestic LPG Refills from 1 October 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas

Biometric Aadhaar Authentication Mandatory for Subsidised Domestic LPG Refills from 1 October 2026

27.43 crore consumers (89.9 per cent) have already completed authentication and need not do anything further

Authentication can be completed at the time of delivery, at the distributor’s showroom, or on OMC mobile apps

19 SEP 2026 7:42PM by PIB Delhi

From 1 October 2026, domestic LPG consumers will need to have completed Biometric Aadhaar Authentication (BAA) to book refills at the regulated Retail Selling Price (RSP) with applicable subsidy.

BAA ensures that subsidised LPG reaches only genuine and deserving households. Linking each connection to the Aadhaar-authenticated consumer helps prevent diversion of subsidised domestic cylinders for commercial and industrial use, removes duplicate and ineligible connections, and makes subsidy delivery transparent and targeted. The process is not meant to deny LPG to any genuine household, and every eligible consumer has several easy ways to complete it.

What changes from 1 October 2026

Consumers who have already completed BAA do not need to do it again. Their refills continue as before.

For consumers who have not completed BAA, refill booking at RSP with subsidy will be enabled once authentication is completed.

How to complete BAA

During refill delivery: the delivery person can complete authentication on the spot using the OMC mobile application.

At the distributor’s showroom: consumers can visit their LPG distributor and complete authentication there.

On OMC mobile apps: consumers can complete the process themselves from home using:

IndianOil ONE for Indane customers

HelloBPCL for Bharatgas customers

HP PAY for HP Gas customers

Video tutorials on completing self e-KYC are available on the PMUY portal.

Option for consumers who do not wish to complete BAA

Consumers who are unwilling or unable to complete BAA can still receive LPG. They will need to register this choice on their OMC’s digital channels: the consumer web portal, mobile app, WhatsApp chatbot, IVRS or other available channels.

These consumers will be supplied LPG applicable market price, without any subsidy, in 5 kg or 10 kg cylinders, subject to local availability with the OMC.

As on 19 September 2026, 27.43 crore active domestic LPG consumers have completed BAA, a coverage of 89.9 per cent.

Consumers were first asked to complete BAA by 30 June 2026. The deadline was extended several times to give consumers more time: to 31 July, 7 August, 15 August, 23 August, 31 August, 7 September and finally 14 September 2026.

Since October 2023, Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have run a nationwide outreach drive. More than 12 crore SMS and WhatsApp messages have been sent. Distributors and delivery staff have followed up individually with consumers yet to authenticate. Special camps have been held at distributorships, high-footfall locations and in rural areas. IVRS prompts during refill booking, mobile notifications, and campaigns on social media, in newspapers and through other channels have also been used.

The cost of LPG subsidy

Domestic LPG is sold below cost. The implicit subsidy for September 2026 is around ₹210 per 14.2 kg cylinder; in June 2026 it reached ₹721 per cylinder.

To keep domestic LPG affordable, the Government paid OMCs compensation of ₹22,000 crore in FY 2022-23 and is paying ₹30,000 crore during FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27. Even after this, accumulated under-recoveries of public sector OMCs on domestic LPG exceeded ₹62,000 crore as on 31 August 2026. Directing the subsidy only to genuine consumers is essential to sustaining it.

Complete BAA before 1 October

Consumers who have not yet completed BAA are urged to do so before 1 October 2026 through any of the channels above, available in both urban and rural areas.

For assistance with LPG services, consumers may call the toll-free helpline 1800 2333 555.

headline: Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol addresses the inauguration ceremony of the new Head Office of Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society Limited in Belagavi, Karnataka
fullText:

Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol addresses the inauguration ceremony of the new Head Office of Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society Limited in Belagavi, Karnataka

​​​​​​​Under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, the cooperative sector of the country is continuously getting strengthened: Shri Murlidhar Mohol

More than 160 important decisions have been taken in the cooperative sector under the leadership of Shri Amit Shah; work worth approximately Rs 3,000 crore has been initiated for computerisation of nearly 80,000 PACS: Shri Mohol

Nearly 70,000 cooperative institutions have joined the three national-level Multi-State Cooperative Societies; village-level cooperative institutions have been linked with more than 25 types of business activities

Cooperative banking is gaining new strength through the Umbrella Organisation for Urban Cooperative Banks and the ‘Sahkar Sarathi’ platform for Rural Cooperative Banks

Cooperative sector will require approximately 17 lakh trained human resources over the next 10 years; ‘Tribhuvan’ Sahkari University is an important initiative in this direction: Shri Mohol

New initiatives such as White Revolution, Sahkar Bima and Bharat Taxi are continuously expanding the scope of cooperation: Shri Mohol

Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society has approximately 4.60 lakh members, 263 branches across the country and a business of more than Rs 9,000 crore

19 SEP 2026 7:16PM by PIB Delhi

Under Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’ and the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah, continuous efforts are being made to strengthen, modernise, make transparent and expand the cooperative sector of the country. In this sequence, Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol today addressed the inauguration ceremony of the new Head Office of Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society Limited (Multi-State), located at Nandi in Chikodi Taluka of Belagavi district, Karnataka. Union Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi, several dignitaries from the State of Karnataka, representatives of the cooperative sector and a large number of citizens were present on the occasion.

Addressing the gathering on the occasion, Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Shri Murlidhar Mohol said that today is an extremely important and joyous day for the cooperative sector in Karnataka. Shri Mohol conveyed his best wishes to the entire team of the institution on behalf of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah and the Union Ministry of Cooperation.

The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that Shri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society has approximately 4.60 lakh members, its 263 branches are spread across the country and the Society has a business of more than Rs 9,000 crore. He said that today also marks the 36th Foundation Day of the institution. He congratulated the entire team of the institution for managing cooperative activities on such a large scale.

Shri Mohol said that cooperation has expanded on a large scale in States such as Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu. He said that Shri Annasaheb Jolle and his wife have made an important contribution to the cooperative sector of Karnataka. Referring to the work carried out by them in various areas, including cooperative sugar factories, cooperative banks and credit societies, Shri Mohol appreciated their contribution.

The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji deserves appreciation for giving a new direction to the cooperative system of the country. He said that today more than 8.5 lakh cooperative societies and cooperative institutions are functioning in the country and approximately 32 crore people are members of these cooperative institutions. Nearly 20 to 25 crore families are directly connected with cooperation and, thus, almost half of the country’s population is associated with the cooperative system in one form or another.

Shri Mohol said that earlier, the work relating to cooperation in the country was handled under a department of the agriculture sector within the jurisdiction of a Joint Secretary. Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji, recognising the scale and importance of the cooperative sector, established an independent Ministry of Cooperation in the country. He said that over the last nearly five years, the cooperative sector of the country has undergone a fundamental transformation under the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah.

Shri Mohol said that Shri Amit Shah has vast experience of working across the cooperative banking system, from village societies to district banks and State-level cooperative banks. Under his leadership as the country’s first Minister of Cooperation, cooperation in India received a new momentum and work began towards its equitable expansion and development across the country.

The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that more than 160 important decisions have been taken for the cooperative sector during the tenure of Shri Amit Shah. He said that through these decisions, efforts have been made to strengthen and empower the cooperative movement of the country. Work worth approximately Rs 3,000 crore has been initiated for the computerisation of nearly 80,000 village-level Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS). In addition, village cooperative institutions have been linked with 25 different types of businesses to expand their economic activities and sources of income.

Shri Mohol said that three Multi-State Cooperative Societies have been created with the objective of developing a comprehensive cooperative ecosystem for farmers and nearly 70,000 cooperative institutions across the country have joined them as members. He said that through this, work is being undertaken to provide new opportunities to farmers and cooperative institutions.

The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that there are more than 1,500 Urban Cooperative Banks in the country. Earlier, there was no common organisation to understand the difficulties and problems faced by these banks, address issues related to the Reserve Bank of India and facilitate their business operations. He said that for this purpose, an Umbrella Organisation, NUCFDC, has been established in the country, through which assistance is being provided to ensure the smooth functioning of Urban Cooperative Banks.

Shri Mohol said that an independent platform named ‘Sahkar Sarathi’ has been developed for Rural Cooperative Banks. He said that keeping future requirements in mind, there is a need to take cooperation to every part of the country, further expand its reach, make the functioning of cooperative institutions more systematic and efficient, and further strengthen trust and credibility in the cooperative system.

The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation said that approximately 17 lakh people will need to be trained to work in the cooperative sector over the next nearly 10 years. He said that with this objective, the country’s first cooperative university, ‘Tribhuvan’ Sahkari University, has been launched, which will play an important role in developing trained human resources for the cooperative sector.

Shri Mohol said that renewed work has also begun in the field of the White Revolution. Along with this, several new initiatives such as Sahkar Bima and Bharat Taxi have been launched under the guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji and the leadership of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Shri Amit Shah. He said that through these initiatives, the cooperative sector of the country is continuously becoming stronger.

The Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation, referring to the role of the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC), said that NCDC provides assistance and financial support to cooperative institutions across the country. He underlined the importance of NCDC in providing financial and institutional support to cooperative institutions. Shri Mohol expressed confidence that the cooperative movement would continue to progress in the same manner throughShri Beereshwar Co-operative Credit Society. He said that such cooperative institutions have an important role in truly realising and fulfilling the resolve of ‘Sahkar se Samriddhi’.

headline: NLC India: Powering National Growth Through Energy Security and Sustainability
fullText:
Ministry of Coal

NLC India: Powering National Growth Through Energy Security and Sustainability

19 SEP 2026 6:40PM by PIB Delhi

As India moving towards becoming a developed economy by 2047, reliable and sustainable power holds the key for national growth. Navigating the dual imperative of uncompromised baseload energy and ambitious decarbonisation, NLC India Limited (NLCIL)—a Navratna enterprise under the Ministry of Coal with existing power generation capacity of 8,405 MW and Mining Capacity of 59.10 MTPA at present—is redefining its identity from a legacy mining enterprise to rapidly evolving into an integrated, future-ready energy powerhouse backing India's Panchamrit climate goals.

Energy Security: Reliable energy is critical to economic expansion, and coal and lignite continue to serve as the nation's baseload anchor. To meet India's power requirements sustainably, NLCIL is expanding its mining footprint responsibly while modernizing generation:

Capacity Scaling: Increasing total mining capacity from 59.1 MTPA to 104.35 MTPA by 2030, targeting 115.85 MTPA by 2047 to avoid import dependence.

High-Efficiency, Low-Emission (HELE) Generation: Transitioning to cleaner thermal power with supercritical units at Ghatampur (1,980 MW) and ultra-supercritical pit-head thermal power projects at Talabira (2,400 MW) and Machhakatta (4,000 MW), drastically minimizing specific coal consumption and emissions.

Logistical Efficiency via FMC: Commissioning 63.5 MTPA capacity across First Mile Connectivity (FMC) rail corridors at Pachwara South, North Dhadu (west), Talabira, Machhakatta and New Patrapara (South) to eliminate road transport emissions/ oil dependency, thus improving logistical efficiency.

Renewable Energy: NLCIL is actively developing India's clean energy through its dedicated green arm, NLCIL Renewables Limited (NIRL):

10 GW by 2030: Growing its operational renewable portfolio from ~1.8 GW to over 10 GW by 2030 (scaling to 32.7 GW by 2047), establishing a 50% clean energy mix in its generation well ahead of schedule.

Battery Energy Storage System (BESS): Projects under development includes 250 MW / 500 MWh in Tamil Nadu, 300 MW / 1,800 MWh with SECI in Rajasthan, 275 MW / 550 MWh with GUVNL in Gujarat and 50 MW / 200 MWh with WBSEDL.

Pumped Storage Projects (PSP): Targeting large-scale storage assets in Tamil Nadu and Odisha to balance renewable grid intermittency.

Other Diversification Projects: To safeguard India from global supply chain disruptions and to achieve low-carbon industrialization, NLCIL is implementing the following:

Green Hydrogen & CCS: Constructing a pilot 4 MW solar-powered PEM electrolyzer Green Hydrogen plant at Neyveli and partnering with IIT Madras on advanced Carbon Capture Systems.

Strategic Mineral Autonomy: Currently, NLCIL has secured domestic composite exploration licenses for phosphorite, limestone in Chhattisgarh and vanadium, titanium in Telangana states. Also pursuing international prospects through KABIL for critical minerals.

By aligning with national self-reliance (Aatmanirbhar Bharat), NLC India Limited is ensuring Nation’s energy security today, while laying a robust foundation for low carbon emission revenue businesses/ initiatives for tomorrow.

headline: From Alcohol Dependence to a Life of Dignity: Dara Singh's Journey of Recovery
fullText:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment

From Alcohol Dependence to a Life of Dignity: Dara Singh's Journey of Recovery

19 SEP 2026 5:52PM by PIB Delhi

Timely treatment, counselling and rehabilitation support can help a person overcome dependence on drugs and psychotropic substances, restore family ties and return to a productive life.

Substance dependence can severely affect an individual's health, relationships, livelihood and place within the community.

Dara Singh (name changed), a 29-year-old self-employed man from Dausa district, Rajasthan, overcame years of alcohol dependence with treatment and rehabilitation support from Nasha Mukti Kendra, Didwana, an Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts. He is now completely abstinent, has rebuilt his family relationships and earns approximately Rs. 500 per day through self-employment.

For several years, alcohol dependence affected Dara Singh's physical and mental health and disrupted his daily life. He experienced emotional instability, stress and reduced self-esteem, while his family faced conflict, social stigma and growing financial pressure. As household resources were increasingly diverted towards alcohol, the family's economic condition became unstable and his relationships within the family and community deteriorated.

Despite these difficulties, Dara Singh wanted to regain a stable and healthy life, rebuild his family's trust, become financially independent and reintegrate into society. His family remained supportive and sought professional assistance when the impact of alcohol dependence became increasingly severe.

He was admitted to Nasha Mukti Kendra, Didwana, where he actively followed the centre's routine and participated in counselling sessions, yoga, medical care and rehabilitation activities. Daily counselling, behavioural guidance and awareness about productive activities and livelihood opportunities helped him understand the consequences of substance use and develop healthier habits. Regular follow-up interventions further supported his recovery and encouraged him to remain committed to an alcohol-free life.

After successfully completing treatment, follow-up visits and assessments recorded continued positive progress. His health and behaviour improved significantly, and he completely abstained from alcohol. He now stays away from negative influences, maintains healthy relationships with his family and has successfully reintegrated into society.

Dara Singh has resumed self-employment and earns approximately Rs. 500 per day. His income enables him to contribute to his household and move towards financial independence. His recovery has also restored peace within the family and helped rebuild the trust and respect affected by his dependence.

Extending his gratitude Dara Singh said, “The treatment and counselling gave me the strength to leave alcohol behind and begin my life again. Today, I am healthy, earning for my family and living with dignity."

Dara Singh's journey demonstrates how family support, professional counselling, medical care and sustained rehabilitation can help a person overcome substance dependence and return to a healthy, productive and dignified life.

headline: Ministry of Ayush Advances Artificial Intelligence for Ayurveda and Traditional Medicine
fullText:
Ministry of Ayush Advances Artificial Intelligence for Ayurveda and Traditional Medicine

19 SEP 2026 5:30PM by PIB Delhi

Building on the digital foundation laid by Ayush Grid, the Ministry of Ayush is now advancing Artificial Intelligence as the next frontier for Ayurveda and the wider Ayush sector. The Ministry has been exploring AI across healthcare, research, education, information services and investment facilitation, with an emerging ecosystem that includes both specialised AI applications and broader collaborations with national AI initiatives.

At the citizen-facing level, the MAISP Chatbot is designed to make Ayush-related information, including Ayurveda, readily accessible through a conversational interface. The ARP Research Assistant, a GenAI-based assistant, extends the Ayush Research Portal, helping researchers navigate Ayurveda and other Ayush literature more effectively. The eLMS Chatbot introduces AI-based Student Life Cycle Management for Ayurveda and other Ayush education institutions, while the e-CHARAK Chatbot functions as a medicinal-plant trade assistant, connecting conversational AI with the ecosystem that underpins Ayurvedic pharmacology. Yoga Saarthi serves as a yoga recommendation AI chatbot, and Nivesh Saarthi serves as an AI assistant for investment in the Ayush sector. Together, these chatbots demonstrate the expansion of Ayush Grid from digital portals towards interactive, intelligent and user-oriented AI services.

At the IndiaAI Impact Summit 2026, the AI Impact Casebook on Health, developed in partnership with the World Health Organization, featured a dedicated snapshot from the Ministry of Ayush titled "AI-driven Decision Support for Ayurveda: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Approach." The inclusion of this Ayurveda use case in a global health AI casebook underscores the potential of Generative AI and RAG to strengthen evidence-based Ayurvedic knowledge and the wider digital transformation of traditional medicine.

The Ministry's broader AI ecosystem is being advanced through participation in the IndiaAI Innovation Challenge, with a focus on developing AI-enabled solutions tailored to the Ayush sector. Key use cases include voice-based Electronic Health Records, disease-trend detection, and personalised treatment-support solutions, aimed at leveraging Artificial Intelligence to enhance healthcare delivery, clinical insights and patient-centric care across Ayurveda and other Ayush systems.

On 11 July 2025, the WHO, ITU and WIPO jointly released a technical brief, Mapping the Application of Artificial Intelligence in Traditional Medicine, examining how AI can support traditional medicine while highlighting the importance of responsible, evidence-informed and culturally appropriate approaches, including for Ayurveda.

The Ministry of Ayush has collaborated with IndiaAI and the Digital India Bhashini Division (DIBD), MeitY, creating opportunities to explore artificial intelligence, language technologies, digital health and advanced computing for the Ayush ecosystem. Ministry artefacts are now available on AI Kosh to support wider AI research and dissemination in the Ayush and Ayurveda domains. Through the Bhashini collaboration, Ayush Grid portals, including those serving Ayurveda practitioners, students and citizens, are now available in 22 scheduled languages of India, enabling wider participation and reach across the country's linguistic diversity.

With AI assistants alongside collaborations involving IndiaAI and Bhashini, the Ayush ecosystem is moving further towards intelligent and citizen-centric digital services. The intent is not to replace traditional Ayurvedic knowledge with technology, but to use Artificial Intelligence to strengthen, connect and amplify that knowledge, making it more discoverable, evidence-based and accessible to citizens in India and around the world.

headline: Union Minister of State for Communications Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani Addresses Rozgar Mela in Chennai
fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of State for Communications Dr Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani Addresses Rozgar Mela in Chennai

Dr Pemmasani Exhorts New Recruits to identify challenges faced by citizens and explore solutions through technology, innovation and entrepreneurship

Union MoS Highlights India’s transformation in manufacturing, infrastructure, digital governance and telecom connectivity since 2014 under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi

More than 51,000 candidates receive appointment letters across the country under the nationwide Rozgar Mela

19 SEP 2026 5:08PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development, Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, while addressing the 20th Rozgar Mela in Chennai today, congratulated the newly appointed government employees and their families, calling upon the recruits to approach public service with integrity, empathy, responsibility and a commitment to continuous learning.

Dr. Pemmasani said the occasion marked an important milestone not only for the recruits but also for their families, who had supported them through examinations and the recruitment process. He said securing a government job remains an important aspiration for many young Indians and congratulated the recruits selected from among more than 51,000 candidates receiving appointment letters across the country under the nationwide Rozgar Mela.

With the completion of the 20th Rozgar Mela, around 12.75 lakh young people will have received appointment letters through the initiative.

Sharing his journey from a modest family background to becoming a doctor, entrepreneur and public representative, Dr. Pemmasani emphasised the importance of learning, adaptability and perseverance. He encouraged the newly appointed employees to seek guidance from experienced colleagues and make effective use of digital learning resources and AI tools.

The Union Minister of State urged the recruits to remain open to new postings, languages, cultures and working environments, saying that exposure to unfamiliar surroundings can help build confidence and broaden their understanding of the country.

Emphasising the human dimension of government service, Dr. Pemmasani said employees should not allow routine administrative work to diminish their sense of purpose. A government employee may view a file as routine administrative work, but for the citizen concerned, it could represent an important aspect of their life.

The Union MoS urged the recruits to question established practices, verify facts and avoid blindly following processes simply because they are widely followed. “Just because 100 people do the wrong thing, that doesn’t make it a right thing,” he said, emphasising the importance of integrity and sound decision-making.

Speaking about India’s transformation since 2014 under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi , Dr. Pemmasani highlighted the changes in governance, infrastructure, technology and public service delivery. He said India’s mobile manufacturing ecosystem has expanded from just two manufacturing units in 2014-15 to around 300 today. Mobile phone production has also increased substantially.

The Minister of State said the transformation is equally visible in infrastructure. The national highway network has expanded significantly. Railway electrification has progressed rapidly. Vande Bharat trains and railway station redevelopment are improving connectivity and passenger experience.

He also highlighted the growth of indigenous defence production. India’s defence exports have increased from around ₹600 crore in 2013-14 to around ₹30,000 crore in 2025-26.

Furthermore, the Minister of State encouraged the young employees to identify challenges faced by citizens and explore solutions through technology, innovation and entrepreneurship.

Towards the conclusion of his address, Dr. Pemmasani outlined three things for the recruits to remember throughout their careers: the citizen, their families and their younger selves. He said these principles would help them remain grounded and committed to public service. Looking towards 2047, he urged the newly appointed employees to continuously reflect on whether they are living up to the trust placed in them by the country, their families and the citizens they serve.

Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani concluded his address by congratulating the newly appointed employees and wishing them success in their careers and service to the nation.

Indian Railways Approves ₹209 Crore for Electronic Interlocking at 7 Stations in Solapur Division

19 SEP 2026 4:15PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Railways has approved the provision of Electronic Interlocking (EI) at seven stations of Solapur Division of Central Railway at a total cost of ₹209 crore.

The approved work involves provision of Electronic Interlocking at Mohol, Mundhewadi, Bale, Solapur, Hotgi Junction-Hotgi A Cabin, Shahabad and Wadi Junction on the High Density Network (HDN) 7 route, where Kavach, Automatic Block Signalling (ABS) and Centralised Traffic Control (CTC) works have been sanctioned.

The modern signalling system will strengthen railway signalling infrastructure across the division and facilitate the implementation of Kavach, the indigenous Automatic Train Protection system.

Electronic Interlocking is a modern computer-based signalling system that replaces conventional relay-based interlocking. It provides more reliable control of points and signals, enables faster fault detection and restoration, facilitates easier maintenance and supports more efficient train operations.

The project is part of Indian Railways’ continuing efforts to modernise signalling infrastructure, strengthen railway safety and improve operational efficiency across high-density routes.
